newsitem.title: PERU: Peru proposes $2.482 bln buyback under Brady plan.
newsitem.headline: Peru proposes $2.482 bln buyback under Brady plan.

text.p: The Peruvian government has formally proposed to its bank creditors a $2.482 billion buyback at the closing of its Brady plan to restructure $10.657 billion of foreign debt, a senior Economy Ministry source said Friday.
Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress earlier this week the buyback negotiations involved $1.265 billion of principal and $1.217 billion of interest.
"We have announced this proposal to the banks. The idea is to buy back these sums at the closing of the deal," the ministry source told Reuters.
Of the total $10.657 billion included in the Brady deal, $6.476 billion is interest and $4.181 billion principal, according to the ministry.

Camet said earlier this week the total would be reduced after the closing of the deal to Brady bonds "with a nominal value of $4.604 billion," including $3.809 billion of interest and the rest principal.

A second Economy Ministry official, who asked not to be named, explained Friday that the majority of the reduced debt would be interest because "this is the most difficult part to reduce in the negotiations."

The senior source said the ongoing negotiations with creditor banks to finalize bond selections under the Brady plan were centering on three areas: financing the deal; the "painful reconciliation" process of fixing the precise amounts of principal and interest owed to each institution; and the drafting of the banks' bond choice proposals.
"We hope to finish as soon as we can, but it is a complicated process with a lot of money involved," he said.
Peru had originally announced a July 31 deadline for banks to choose their bond options and an August 9 date for the government to accept them formally.
However, the negotiations have dragged on in recent weeks without an official explanation for the delay.
The formal closing of the deal will follow the finalization of bond negotiations with the banks.
